prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators, and its first experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I opened with IceCube (B024) first, and I still regard it as a first-rank instrumental and scientific achievement. After reading the eight ballots, however, I move my preferred configuration to topological insulators. B009 is the only candidate that seven of eight members place in their top three, and the support comes from members with very different fields: Danielsson and Mehlig rank it first, while Johansson, Lindroth and Olsson rank it second and Eriksson and Kroll third. Convergence of this kind from condensed-matter, atomic and theory perspectives is not proof of merit, but the underlying case stands on its own. The prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and the Z2 classification by Kane and Mele is original and changed how band structure is classified. Molenkamp's group then provided an unambiguous experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells. Confirmation in many independent materials and over about two decades makes the result mature. The theory-plus-experiment split into three names is cleaner than for most competing candidates, which matters because attribution is the main weakness of IceCube (single name), theta13 (collaborations plus T2K), optical-lattice simulation (five names) and trapped ions (overlap with 2012).
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. The Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal that identified HgTe was the immediate trigger for Molenkamp's experiment and is not among the credited names, and Hasan's three-dimensional ARPES work is excluded by a three-person limit, so the trio is defensible but leaves out serious claimants. A second reservation is novelty: the 2016 prize recognised topological phase transitions and phases of matter, and Kroll rightly notes that some will see this as a follow-on. Finally, as an experimentalist I note that direct technological payoff is still limited, unlike a measurement such as IceCube that opens a new observational window.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks topological insulators first as a new classification of quantum phases by band topology, with a natural theory-plus-experiment trio of Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, while acknowledging that the BHZ proposal is outside the credited names.
responses.response: I agree with the ranking and the trio, and Danielsson's view that the idea is conceptually clean is what moved me. I would press the BHZ point harder than the opening ballot does. If the committee cannot credit BHZ, the citation should be written around the quantum spin Hall prediction and its first realisation rather than around the HgTe proposal, so it does not imply credit we cannot give. I do not agree with the implied view that this makes the attribution unproblematic; it is only the least problematic of the options.

responses.point: Kroll ranks B026 first and B009 third. He regards B009 as a distinct and mature follow-on to the 2016 topological-phases prize, though some may see it as incremental.
responses.response: Kroll's incrementalism concern is the one I take most seriously, because 2016 honoured topological phase transitions and topological phases in matter. I think the answer is that the 2016 work concerned theory of topological order in specific models, whereas Kane-Mele's Z2 invariant and the HgTe realisation introduced time-reversal-invariant topological insulators with a measurable edge signature. That is a different step, but I concede it is a judgment and not a settled fact. I also disagree with Kroll's first place for optical lattice clocks only mildly: I accept that the metrological case is strong, but it was supported by only three members and I do not see broader backing for it.

responses.point: Johansson ranks circuit QED first and topological insulators second. She sees circuit QED as an original, cleanly demonstrated platform behind leading quantum processors, though the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is close in subject.
responses.response: I agree that circuit QED is a very strong achievement, and I ranked it fourth. My difficulty is the same one she raises, the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits, which makes a prize this year look like too close a follow-up and complicates who is credited. Her own second choice is the one I now prefer, and I would ask whether she sees the 2025 overlap as disqualifying for B010 this year or only a timing question that could be revisited.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks DMFT first and tunnel magnetoresistance second, placing topological insulators third as a coherent Kane-Mele-Molenkamp trio with durable concepts but limited direct technological payoff.
responses.response: I accept Eriksson's point that topological insulators are a showcase for first-principles materials theory, which strengthens the case. On B014 I have no strong objection to the science, but I am not persuaded by the attribution: he himself notes that Metzner is not credited and the credit is spread over more than three people. On B045 the independent Miyazaki and Moodera results and the later MgO work make a clean split harder than for B009, and the 2007 GMR prize adds the same overlap concern.

uncertainties: Whether the BHZ proposers or Hasan should displace one of the three credited names, which this list's credited names do not allow
Whether the 2016 prize makes a topological-insulator prize read as incremental to the full committee
Whether IceCube credit could be resolved with names beyond Francis Halzen, which would change my preference
Whether the 2025 superconducting-circuits prize rules circuit QED out for this year or only delays it
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B009. My documented collaborations (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+, XL-Calibur) are in astroparticle physics and instrumentation. Candidate B024 (IceCube) is in my general research area, but no documented collaboration or personal tie to IceCube or Francis Halzen is recorded, so I flag proximity only.
